propositions: The file test_concurrency_regression.py contains 23 sites where _expire_sync_marker and _engine_run pairs establish fixture preconditions or test behavior via incidental sync operations that can silently fail under best-effort read semantics.

Eight of these 23 sites (Kind P) are load-bearing fixture preconditions where a sync must succeed deterministically; they have been converted to use the checked _sync_from_origin helper (fetch + ff-only merge) to eliminate silent failures.

Fifteen of the 23 sites (Kind R) deliberately drive reconvergence through the production read path as the behavior under test itself; these retain _engine_run and are now routed through a named _reconverge_by_read_sync helper to document why the best-effort contract is appropriate.

Under REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off, the converted preconditions still land reliably with the best-effort read path disabled, proving the checked fetch+merge strategy fixes the flake mechanism without masking true invariant failures.

Raw git push operations in the file remain a separate unexamined category (18 sites) distinct from the sync-by-side-effect pattern, potentially contributing to races in the tickets-store write-lock retry path.
